subject.title: refactor(qa): finish Matrix QA Lab ownership

question: After https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103604 lands, should the exact-head removal of the source-only @openclaw/qa-matrix package and private QA Lab facade be approved as the final ownership cutover?
rationale: The implementation and proof are strong, but deleting a plugin/runtime compatibility surface and authorizing the dependency graph change are intentional repository-owner decisions that automation cannot make.

options.title: Authorize the ordered cutover
options.body: Land the predecessor first, confirm the final head still preserves both Matrix scenario catalogs and redirects, then approve the package and lockfile removal.

options.title: Retain the shim temporarily
options.body: Keep the compatibility package and facade until a concrete source-checkout consumer audit or a later coordinated cleanup establishes that removal is safe.

options.title: Pause the final stack layer
options.body: Leave this PR open without landing if the predecessor changes or the dependency removal cannot receive exact-head authorization.

recommendation.title: Authorize the ordered cutover
recommendation.body: Land the predecessor first, confirm the final head still preserves both Matrix scenario catalogs and redirects, then approve the package and lockfile removal.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the migration stack and the prior merged QA Lab evidence architecture, making them the best coordinator for ordered landing and final-head confirmation, while an eligible administrator or security reviewer supplies the required authorization.
